ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The curved surfaces of two identical cylinders are cut open along the vertical dotted line, as shown and then stuck together to create the curved surface of one big cylinder. What can be said about the volume of the resulting cylinder compared to the volume of one of the small cylinders?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure there are two identical small cylinders, and on the side surface of each cylinder there is a vertical dashed line, indicating cutting open along the vertical direction. In the middle there is an arrow pointing to the right side. The right side shows a wider cylinder, whose height looks the same as that of the small cylinders on the left, indicating that after the curved surfaces of the two small cylinders are unfolded, they are pasted side by side together to form the curved surface of a large cylinder. Reasoning: Let the radius of each small cylinder be r, and the height be h. After the curved surface of one small cylinder is unfolded, it is a rectangle with height h and width 2πr. After two identical curved surfaces are pasted side by side together, the width becomes 4πr, and the height is still h. This width is the circumference of the large cylinder, so 2πR = 4πr, obtaining the large cylinder radius R = 2r. The volume of the large cylinder is π(2r)^2h = 4πr^2h, while the volume of one small cylinder is πr^2h. Therefore the volume of the large cylinder is 4 times the volume of one small cylinder.

How many times as large is the volume of the resulting cylinder compared to the volume of one of the small cylinders?

method.method_draft: Read the image as showing two congruent small cylinders, each cut vertically along a dotted line, and then their lateral curved surfaces joined side-by-side to form the lateral surface of one larger cylinder of the same height. Let one small cylinder have radius r and height h, so its curved surface unwraps to a rectangle of height h and width 2πr. Joining two identical curved surfaces gives a rectangle of height h and width 4πr, which becomes the big cylinder's circumference. Thus 2πR = 4πr, so R = 2r while the height remains h. Compare volumes: big volume = π(2r)^2h = 4πr^2h, which is 4 times the volume of one small cylinder.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中左侧有两个相同的小圆柱，每个圆柱的侧面都有一条竖直虚线，表示沿竖直方向剪开。中间有箭头指向右侧。右侧显示一个更宽的圆柱，其高度看起来与左侧小圆柱相同，表示把两个小圆柱的曲面展开后并排粘在一起形成一个大圆柱的曲面。

推理：设每个小圆柱半径为 r，高为 h。一个小圆柱的曲面展开后是高为 h、宽为 2πr 的长方形。两个相同曲面并排粘在一起后，宽变为 4πr，高仍为 h。这个宽度就是大圆柱的周长，所以 2πR = 4πr，得到大圆柱半径 R = 2r。大圆柱体积为 π(2r)^2h = 4πr^2h，而一个小圆柱体积为 πr^2h。因此大圆柱的体积是一个小圆柱体积的 4 倍。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is the direct net/circumference route: use the visual cut-and-join operation to infer that the lateral-surface width, hence circumference, doubles, then apply the cylinder volume formula. It is the natural single solution path for this problem.
planner_metadata.image_role: The image shows two identical cylinders on the left, each with a vertical dotted cut line, an arrow, and one wider cylinder on the right whose height matches the small cylinders and whose curved surface is formed from the two small surfaces.
planner_metadata.text_role: The text states that the curved surfaces of two identical cylinders are cut open along the dotted vertical line and stuck together to make the curved surface of one big cylinder, and asks for the volume ratio relative to one small cylinder.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use the cylinder lateral surface net: unwrapped curved surface width equals circumference 2πr and height is unchanged. Use cylinder volume V = πr^2h, so doubling the circumference doubles the radius and therefore quadruples the volume when height stays the same.
